- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is significantly above recent mean, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) and forecast is below recent mean, increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike, reduce forecast by 10–20% in the next 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true outcome by >5% over 3–5 days, apply a downward bias correction of 2–5% per day.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is volatile, smooth transitions by averaging 2–3 prior days’ values before projecting.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates from forecast by >10% in first 5 days, adjust forecast downward for remaining days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment after a spike, assume downward momentum and reduce forecast slope.
